item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Oditi marks four distinct points $S$, $T$, $U$ and $V$ on her paper. No three of the points lie on one straight path. The diagram shows the points.

Which claim correctly counts the distinct lines fixed by those points?

options.A: Six lines: each pair among $S$, $T$, $U$ and $V$ determines exactly one line.
options.B: One line, because any set of points always lies on a single line.
options.C: Infinitely many lines, because one point alone already fixes infinitely many lines.
options.D: Sixteen lines, by multiplying four points by four possible directions.
